notes: These cells are unfilled both in the historical appendix and in Lasry et al. Table 2 / Lasry dissertation Table 6.2, not merely unknown to the 1918 analysts. Baseline fills remain separate hypotheses unless an independent constraint supports them.

An illustrative square in paper Figure 2 / dissertation Figure 6.2 places VF=6 and XA=5, opposite the baseline fill. It also prints N twice (AX and XG), contradicting the final key table. Treat the two digits as unresolved, rather than elevating the inconsistent illustrative figure to an established key.

limits: This is a partial ordinary-word proposal, not recovery of a complete message. Its title, name-like field, destination/preposition and footer retain the exact raw output.
The readable excerpt omits positions 5–30,39–53 and86–94 without supplying any word, place or numeral.
Rastatt, Zimmermann and a full title expansion are unselected. No same-message copy or historical identification is claimed.
Exactly three slots are added under the advertised190-slot hypothesis. No printed slot is excluded, moved or copied, and the Nov7–9 key remains unchanged.
The two unassigned square cells remain globally opposite digits5 and6. Their repeated occurrences are coupled across all modeled positions.
All six minimum-substitution source maps are retained. The displayed primary uses four supplied unknown-coordinate values rather than five, but this does not establish its historical origin map.
